description: A flex-wrap image grid. Use for client logo strips (no labels) or icon-category tiles (with labels). Items always have an image; labels are optional.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors).

title.description: Optional section heading above the grid.

items.description: Array of image items. Each: { image_url: string, image_alt: string, image_id?: number, label?: string }. Omit label for pure logo display; include label for icon+category tiles.

image_alt.description: Alt text. Use the logo or category name; empty string only for decorative images.

image_id.description: Media Library attachment ID (NOT a URL). When it resolves to a real attachment, the image renders responsively with srcset/sizes via wp_get_attachment_image() instead of a single fixed-size . Falls back to image_url when unset or unresolvable. Get an attachment id via the import_media apply.

label.description: Text label below the image. Omit for logo-only rows.

items.conditionality_note: the height cap applied to a logo image is chosen by that item's `label` — 2.5rem labelled, 3rem unlabelled — an item-level condition the clause grammar, which reaches component props only, cannot express. Since #1066 the two caps are two ROLES (`image` and `image-labeled`), each with its own `sizing.max-height`: write both for a flat strip. `--logos-image-size`, which overrode both, is retired

do_not_touch: schema.json without updating this component's README.md and the repo-root AI_CONTEXT.md

retired_props._note: Props this component declared on 1.x that the v2 rebuild retired (#1066). Each value names the v2 surface that replaced it, so a refusal can offer a route instead of a list of live prop names. Guarded by SchemaValidationTest, which fails in BOTH directions: a key here that still exists in props, or a route naming a role this component does not declare, is a test failure rather than a message that lies.
retired_props.theme: the `_band` role, and it takes three groups rather than one. MEASURED at 375/768/1280 before the prop went: `default` painted NOTHING (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, no border on any edge); `muted` painted `@color-surface` plus a 1px solid `@color-border` rule top and bottom; `inverted` painted `@color-bg-inverted` and re-coloured the heading to `@color-bg`. So the tone is `background.fill`, the `muted` framing is `border.width-top` / `width-bottom` = "1px" with `style-top` / `style-bottom` = "solid" and `color` = "@color-border", and the `inverted` ink is `typography.color` on `_band`, which `heading` follows through `currentColor`. WHAT THE ROUTE DOES NOT REACH: `label` pins `@color-muted` as a direct declaration, so a band ink write does not move it — v1's inverted label was `@color-bg` at `opacity: 0.75`, and `opacity` has no UDC group, so it ports as the measured composite `rgb(192, 195, 201)`. The logo images were never re-inked and still are not. `dark` was never an accepted input (removed at #605). Full reasoning in components/logos/README.md.

_band.description: The band itself - the <section>. THE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT v1'S UNTHEMED BAND RENDERED, measured in Chromium at 375/768/1280: the shared band rhythm and nothing else. NO `background.fill` (measured `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`) and NO border (0px/none on all four edges) - both belonged to `.logos--dark` / `.logos--inverted`, the retired `theme` variants. `@pp-band-padding` is a fluid clamp, so the padding needs no breakpoint map even though three different values were measured (53.6 / 68 / 76.8px). `background.position: center` is declared for CONSISTENCY with the other v2 bands rather than as the thing that prevents a top-left crop - the engine's image companions already append `background-position: center` into the AUTHORED block whenever an image is present, and that block is unlayered, so this pp-zero default is unreachable in exactly the scenario it appears to guard. SETTING `typography.color` HERE REACHES THE HEADING AND NOT THE LABELS: `heading` follows it through `currentColor`, but `label` pins `@color-muted` as a direct declaration on the element, and a direct declaration always beats an inherited value regardless of cascade layer. A dark logos band is therefore THREE writes - this role's fill and ink, plus `label` ink - and the images are not one of them, because nothing ever re-inked them.

heading.description: The band heading (an <h2>). ITS `typography.color` IS `currentColor` for the reason table's and embed's are: v1 pinned `var(--logos-heading-color, var(--color-text))` and re-pointed it to `@color-bg` from `.logos--inverted`, both of which retire with the `theme` prop, and `currentColor` reproduces BOTH - `@color-text` on an unauthored band (measured rgb(16, 24, 40), byte-identical) and the band's own ink on a dark one. IT IS NOT CENTRED, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM ITS SIBLING: stats' heading carries `text-align: center` plus auto side margins (issue 367); logos' measured `text-align: start` with `margin-left: 0` at every tier, so this role declares NEITHER. The two components look like twins and differ here, so the asymmetry is stated rather than quietly flattened - an author who wants the stats treatment writes `typography.align` and the two `spacing.margin-*: auto` values, and gets exactly it. NO `font-weight` AND NO `line-height` DEFAULT: measured 650 and 46.08px, both from base.css's `h2` rule rather than logos' own block (rule 2, the global-value cascade lesson).

list.description: The strip - the <ul>. ONLY ITS GAP IS DESIGN: `display: flex`, `flex-wrap: wrap`, `align-items: center`, `justify-content: center` and the zeroed list `padding`/`margin`/`list-style` are the layout affordance and stay in the stylesheet. The gap is the ONE band-level rhythm knob this component has (measured 32px, `@space-lg`), and it is the strip's rhythm rather than the intra-tile nudge - that one belongs to `item-labeled`.

item.description: One logo cell. IT DECLARES NO DEFAULTS, and the empty block is measurement rather than oversight: v1's `.logos__item` rule is `display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center` and nothing else - three structural properties, no design value at all. The role exists so an author can reach a cell (a border, a padded tile, a hover) without the schema pretending it ships a look it does not.

item-labeled.description: A logo cell that carries a text label under the image - the `--labeled` modifier logos.php emits per item when that item has a `label`. Its `gap` is the image-to-label nudge (measured 8px, `@space-sm`) and its `min-width` keeps a labelled tile from collapsing narrower than its caption (measured 96px, 6rem); `flex-direction: column` is what makes it a tile rather than a cell and stays structural. THIS ROLE IS HOW A MIXED STRIP STAYS MIXED: the modifier is per item, so a strip holding both shapes renders both, and a value written here reaches only the labelled half.

image.description: The logo image in an UNLABELLED cell. Its cap is the measured 3rem (48px rendered). `width: auto` and `object-fit: contain` stay structural - they are what stops a logo distorting, not a value to retune. READ `image-labeled` BEFORE SETTING THIS: v1 routed ONE slot at BOTH cap sites with different fallbacks, so setting it collapsed the label-driven switch on purpose. A role carries one default, so the two caps are two roles now and the switch survives by construction - which also means setting THIS one no longer changes the labelled tiles. That is a capability change, stated here rather than discovered.

obligations.why: `image-labeled` selects the same through the labelled variant with a heavier selector, so its max-height default beats a size set here on labelled rows.

image-labeled.description: The logo image in a LABELLED tile, which v1 capped lower than its unlabelled twin so the image and its caption read as one unit (measured 2.5rem / 40px against the plain cell's 3rem / 48px). THE TWO CAPS ARE INDEPENDENT NOW AND v1'S WERE NOT: `--logos-image-size` was one slot read at both sites, so an author who set it flattened the switch deliberately - the schema called two knobs for one visual job a family it was completing rather than extending. The UDC gives a role exactly one default, so preserving the measured switch requires two roles, and `max-height` is a sizing value that the fail-closed structural-CSS lint will not let stay in the stylesheet. The rendered default is byte-identical to v1; what changed is that `make the logos bigger` is now two writes rather than one.

label.description: The caption under a labelled logo. ITS COLOUR IS A DIRECT DECLARATION ON THE ELEMENT, so a `_band` ink write does not reach it - `@color-muted` measures 5.66:1 on the default band and about 3.1:1 on an authored `@color-bg-inverted` one, under the 4.5:1 floor at this 13px size, so a dark band owes this role a write. THE v1 DARK-BAND TREATMENT WAS `@color-bg` AT `opacity: 0.75` AND CANNOT BE PORTED AS WRITTEN: `opacity` is in none of the UDC groups. It ports as the MEASURED COMPOSITE instead - pixel-sampled at rgb(192, 195, 201) on `@color-bg-inverted`. WHY THAT EXACT VALUE: the composite is (192.75, 195.5, 201.75) and Chromium FLOORS each channel, which is why the measured pixel is 192/195/201 rather than the 193/196/202 that round-half-up predicts — measured 10.11:1 on the inverted band. AND THE SUBSTITUTION IS NOT UNIVERSAL, which matters if the label ever holds more than text: `opacity` dimmed the whole BOX including any descendant and any text decoration, while a colour reaches only the text it is set on. For this label they are equivalent because it renders plain text and nothing else; a caption that later carries a link or an icon would need that child re-inked too. This is the same retirement stats' label takes, and the two were ONE assertion until this rebuild (the #577 A-36 row covered both components); they retire together here, which is why the two rebuilds share a PR.
